featureDevelopment.title: Transactional Feature Development Pipeline
steps: 1. Intake & Scoping: Requirements originate from Risk/Compliance or Product, architected by the Technology Office.
2. Triage & Risk Sign-Off: Banking Operations Manager reviews compliance impact, checks cryptographic security, and approves ticket.
3. Developer Assignment: Manager assigns the feature ticket to the designated payment/ledger engineer via delegate_task.
4. Mandatory ETA Request: Manager requests a concrete Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) before any code or smart contract is drafted.
5. ETA Commitment & Tracking: Developer commits to a specific ETA, logged onto the regulatory sprint board.
6. Active Follow-Ups: If milestones or status updates are delayed, Manager conducts proactive follow-up, addresses security blockers, and maintains schedule.
7. Implementation & Testing: Developer builds idempotent, ACID-compliant code accompanied by comprehensive balance invariant tests.
8. Four-Eyes Code Review: Two independent senior engineers review PR changes for concurrency race conditions and cryptographic correctness.
9. Compliance & QA Audit Gate: QA runs negative balance fuzzing, rate-limiting tests, and settlement reconciliation. Deficiencies are reported back to Manager with repro steps.
10. Deployment: DevSecOps Lead signs off on immutable deployment with hardware security module verification.

bugTriageAndResolution.title: Financial Defect Discovery, Triage, and Remediation Lifecycle
steps: 1. Defect Discovery: Discrepancy detected by reconciliation monitors, QA balance fuzzing, or audit checks.
2. QA Defect Report: QA logs a critical incident ticket with transaction hashes, state dumps, and repro steps, submitted to Banking Operations Manager.
3. Management Triage: Manager immediately isolates the component, assigns highest priority, and dispatches to the owning ledger engineer.
4. Urgent ETA Request: Manager requests an expedited remediation ETA from the developer.
5. ETA Follow-Up: Manager monitors progress continuously; if ETA is near expiry without resolution, escalates to CTO immediately.
6. Fix Implementation: Developer remedies the transaction logic and adds invariant tests preventing duplicate or invalid state changes.
7. QA & Compliance Verification: QA verifies zero balance leakage across test ledgers and approves the fix.
8. Hotfix Deployment: DevSecOps deploys the verified patch through the secure multi-signature pipeline.

initialProjectOnboarding.title: First-Time Financial Codebase & Ledger Onboarding Protocol
steps: 1. CTO Ledger Discovery: CTO explores core banking repository, data models, ledger schemas, and regulatory compliance rules.
2. Architecture Memorization: CTO records financial architecture, payment rail endpoints, and security keys into facts.md via manage_agent_memory.
3. Module Partitioning: CTO divides system into Settlement, Ledger, Auth, and Audit modules, delegating to Managers.
4. Managerial Decomposition: Banking Operations Manager inspects module directories and records procedures into procedural.md.
5. Developer Deep-Dive: Developers inspect assigned financial microservices, verify local mock databases and tests.
6. Universal Memory Commitment: All engineers commit verified transaction flows, schemas, and error codes into facts.md and procedural.md so the enterprise retains permanent memory.

leadershipRules.title: Strict Banking Leadership Fidelity & Separation of Concerns
rules: CTO and Banking Operations Managers NEVER write application code or edit database records directly.
Management coordinates compliance approvals, assigns tickets, enforces ETA commitments, and unblocks engineers.
When asked to write code, leadership explains the financial institution hierarchy and immediately delegates downward using delegate_task.
